correctness.rationale: The published equation (2) matches the four equations under review; the fraction bounds specified in the frozen result are its own hypotheses. Adding the two cat equations gives V'=-mu V+gamma S+aI. For a>=0 it is inward or tangent on V=0, as are the other physical faces under the stated positivity and fraction assumptions. The remaining coordinates stay bounded on this region (the environmental coordinate satisfies a linear comparison), so local invariance gives forward invariance for all time. For a<0 the simplex vertex S=V=0,I=1 is strictly outward in V; continuous dependence at a short positive time gives nearby interior starting points that leave too. The endemic stationary equations force O=kI/mu0, M=0, S=d mu0/(beta k), and I=[mu-(mu+gamma)S]/H; substitution proves sufficiency and uniqueness when admissible. H>0, infection is positive precisely above beta_c, and the residual fraction has sign given by a+(gamma-a)S. Hence it is positive automatically when a>=0 in the endemic branch, and when a=-q<0 its nonnegativity is exactly the upper cutoff, with equality allowing V=0. The ordering of the two thresholds is strict because 0<q<mu and gamma>0. These are algebraic and geometric facts about the printed reduced ODE, not the unreduced equations, stability, or an empirical interpretation. The notes and frozen checker were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The result corrects a concrete omission in a published mathematical model: a positive infection coordinate need not give a feasible state, and the face where admissibility is lost is exactly identified. It gives a complete conditional classification for a natural region, rather than an isolated numerical counterexample. It does not establish a real-world threshold, epidemiological calibration, stability, or an intervention.
